descriptionChirho: A healer or medical practitioner; used in the NT both literally (Luke the physician, the woman who spent all on physicians in Mark 5:26) and in Jesus's proverbial saying 'Physician, heal yourself' and 'The healthy have no need of a physician.' Multilingual evidence confirms singular and plural as the same concept: Spanish 'medico/medicos', Hindi 'vaidya/vaidyon', Arabic 'tabibin/atibba'a', Korean 'uisareul/uisadeului', Swahili 'tabibu/madaktari'. The singular (N-GMS, N-VMS, N-NMS) and plural (N-GMP, N-DMP) forms are grammatical number variation of one sense.
